record.paper_title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Finite capacity of horocycle-flow sublevel sets
record.original_question: In the horocycle-flow example, let M be a compact hyperbolic surface of genus at least 2, let σ be its area form, and let H be the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian on T^*M with the twisted symplectic form ω_0 + π^*σ. Example 4.1 shows that the energy level {H = 1} is aperiodic. For energies above that value, do the sublevel domains {H < a} with a > 1 have finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity?

evidence.quote: Example 4.1 (The horocycle flow). Let M be a compact surface of genus g ≥ 2 equipped with a metric of constant negative curvature K = −1. Let σ be the area form on M. Then the Hamiltonian flow on the energy level {H = 1} has no periodic orbits.
For example, it is not known whether in the setting of Example 4.1 the sets {H < a} with a > 1 have finite capacity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g \ge 2$ equipped with a Riemannian metric of constant curvature $-1$, and let $\sigma$ denote its area $2$-form. On the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ with projection $\pi: T^*M \to M$, consider the twisted symplectic form
\[ \omega = \omega_0 + \pi^*\sigma, \]
where $\omega_0 = -d\lambda$ is the canonical symplectic form. Let $H: T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$ be the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian $H(q,p) = \tfrac{1}{2}\|p\|_g^2$ associated with the dual metric on $T^*M$.

Recall that for a symplectic manifold $(W,\omega)$ and an open subset $U \subset W$, the Hofer–Zehnder capacity $c_{HZ}(U,\omega)$ is the supremum of $\max F - \min F$ over compactly supported smooth Hamiltonians $F: U \to \mathbb{R}$ that are constant near the boundary, have only constant fast-periodic orbits (no nonconstant $T$-periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow of $F$ for $0 < T < 1$), and are admissible in the standard sense (attaining their maximum on an open set, etc.).

It is known that the energy level $\{H = 1\}$ in $(T^*M,\omega)$ corresponds to a horocycle flow and carries no periodic orbits.

Question: For every real number $a > 1$, is the Hofer–Zehnder capacity
\[ c_{HZ}\bigl(\{H < a\},\, \omega_0 + \pi^*\sigma\bigr) \]
finite?
artifact.category_tag: Hofer–Zehnder capacity of twisted cotangent bundles
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work on Hofer–Zehnder capacity in twisted (magnetic) tangent bundles over hyperbolic surfaces (e.g., Bimmermann and earlier results of Ginzburg–Gürel, Lu, Schlenk) treats either low energies below the horocycle/Mañé critical value (e.g., $k<1/2$) or strong magnetic fields, which in this normalization corresponds to energies below $1$. Finiteness of the Hofer–Zehnder capacity of the supercritical sublevel sets $\{H<a\}$ with $a>1$ for hyperbolic surfaces does not appear to have been established in the literature; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Hofer-Zehnder capacity for twisted tangent bundles over closed surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Treats arbitrary constant magnetic fields on the two-sphere and strong constant magnetic fields for higher genus surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Results cover the low-energy (subcritical/strong-field) regime, not energies a>1 above the horocycle level.

status_evidence.title: Relative Hofer-Zehnder capacity and periodic orbits in twisted cotangent bundles
status_evidence.snippet: For a hyperbolic surface, the Hofer–Zehnder Γ-semicapacity of the domain bounded by the kinetic energy hypersurface minus the zero section is finite if k<1/2.
status_evidence.claim: Finiteness results are restricted to subcritical energies k<1/2 in this normalization.

status_evidence.title: Hofer–Zehnder capacity of magnetic disc tangent bundles over constant curvature surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Computes Hofer-Zehnder capacity of magnetic disc tangent bundles over constant curvature surfaces via Hamiltonian circle actions.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses the subcritical regime where the magnetic flow is totally periodic, not the supercritical regime a>1.
